svg.title: Three roads: a map of who fits where
svg.desc: Schematic map of the three roads for a small HCC, plus transplantation. Resectable with good liver function — surgical resection remains the default (AASLD 2023, BCLC 2022); up to 2 cm in a needle-reachable position — resection and RFA offer the same survival benefit, and beyond 2 cm resection should be favoured in resectable patients (BCLC 2022); not fit for surgery, not fit for ablation, or firmly declining surgery — the SBRT slot (AASLD: usable for central and perivascular tumours; Taiwan NHI code 37047B, reimbursed since 2015: single lesion up to 5 cm, Child-Pugh A to B, unfit for or failed surgery, embolisation or ablation); a liver that cannot pay (Child-Pugh score 8 or above, uncontrolled ascites or encephalopathy) — avoid external-beam radiotherapy; within the Milan criteria (single tumour up to 5 cm, or up to 3 tumours each up to 3 cm) — transplant assessment must not be skipped, as the only option treating both the cancer and the cirrhosis. The final decision belongs to the multidisciplinary team.

g.text: SIZE × LOCATION × LIVER
Three roads:
a map of who fits where
'All feasible' is not 'all the same' — each road has
its home ground, plus a fourth: transplant. The final
call belongs to the multidisciplinary team.
Resectable with good liver function —
resection remains the default (AASLD / BCLC)
Resectable · good liver
Resection = the default road
AASLD: the curative treatment of choice without
cirrhosis; BCLC: resection first if transplant and
surgery are both options. 'Equal after adjustment'
is not 'skipping surgery is the same' — no RCT.
Up to 2 cm · reachable
Resection or RFA: the same
survival benefit (BCLC 2022)
Beyond 2 cm ablation loses ground — resection
should be favoured in resectable patients.
Unfit to operate or ablate
The SBRT slot — real and large
AASLD: durable local control when ablation is not
feasible; usable for central and perivascular
tumours. NHI 37047B (since 2015): single ≤5 cm,
Child-Pugh A–B, unfit for or failed surgery,
embolisation or ablation. Also for firm refusers.
A liver that cannot pay
Here SBRT is the wrong answer
AASLD: Child-Pugh 8 or above, uncontrolled
ascites or encephalopathy — avoid external-beam
radiotherapy. Restore the liver, or assess transplant.
Within transplant criteria
Transplant must not be skipped
The only option treating cancer and cirrhosis
together. Milan (single ≤5 cm, or ≤3 each ≤3 cm):
4-year survival 75%, recurrence-free 83% (1996).
Local treatment runs alongside assessment.
Read the three dimensions together; for multinodular,
embolisable disease see the TACE and Y-90 article.
Schematic, redrawn from AASLD 2023, BCLC 2022, the NHI
37047B reimbursement criteria (since 2015) and Mazzaferro
1996 | where you land is for the team to judge
